I will manage this year mostly from what has worked on my land, but I will adjust with prices, water, and the yield I want. I have 20 mu under the wheat-maize rotation, with well irrigation, so I do not farm the same way as a rainfed field. I think in terms of yield target and input balance now, not just habit. For winter wheat, I will stay with improved seed, put enough base fertilizer in to avoid weak tillering, and keep nitrogen split so I do not waste too much early but still protect yield. On my ground in Quzhou, wheat cannot be stingy on nitrogen if I want a stable harvest, so I will use about 18 kg nitrogen per mu, 8 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium. I will irrigate three times if water is normal: once for overwintering or before freeze if the soil is short of moisture, once at jointing, and once around grain filling depending on weather. For wheat I will usually spray three times, one herbicide and two disease or insect passes if needed. I will use rotary tillage after maize because it is faster on 20 mu and fits my labor. For summer maize, I will use hybrid seed. Maize responds clearly to fertilizer and water here, especially with wheat-maize rotation and irrigated conditions, so I will not cut too hard. I will put about 20 kg nitrogen per mu, 7 kg phosphorus, and 6 kg potassium. I will keep two irrigations in mind, mainly around big flare to silking and then grain filling if rain is short. Pest control for maize I will keep at two passes in a normal year. For maize I prefer no-tillage seeding into wheat stubble when conditions allow, because it saves time, holds moisture, and lets me catch the sowing window. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than lose yield, because with 20 mu the bigger loss is a poor harvest, not a few extra bags of input.
